summary: Establish Observability Jira space, Confluence template, and rotate Slack bot credentials with channel-archival automation
description:
Background:
We are consolidating observability work into a dedicated Jira project + Confluence template to standardize runbooks, and we need Slack automation to manage bot credentials and archive stale channels. This will help Platform Pods and SRE maintain consistent onboarding and reduce blast radius from long-lived bot tokens.

Request:
1) Create a Jira project named 'Observability Platform' using the internal-support project template but scoped to operations tickets and runbooks.
2) Add a Confluence space template for Incident/Runbook pages pre-populated with checklists, postmortem links, and SLI/SLO sections.
3) Provision cross-pod service account groups in our identity provider for read/write to the Jira project and Confluence space (group naming: obs-pod-<pod-name>-edit).
4) Implement two automations: (a) rotate the Slack bot token used by the observability slack bot on a 90-day schedule with automated secret storage in the KMS; (b) archive Slack channels older than 90 days of inactivity with a 7-day warning message and a re-open workflow.

Deliverables:
- Jira project created with key prefix OBS and default issue types aligned to SRE runbooks and ops tasks.
- Confluence space + page template published and permissioned.
- Identity groups created and invited to the project/space.
- Automation runbooks and a one-click enablement playbook for pods.

Impact:
This affects provisioning for Platform Pods (us-east, eu-west) and the SRE org. Without automation, tokens and stale channels create security and noise issues.
acceptance_criteria:
1) OBS Jira project exists and a test issue can be created by a member of obs-pod-core-edit.
2) Confluence template available under 'Observability' space and can be instantiated.
3) A service account group obs-pod-sre-edit is able to create/modify pages and issues.
4) Demo of Slack bot token rotation (test rotation executed) with secret seen only in KMS audit logs.
5) Channel archival automation runs in staging and archives a test channel after simulated inactivity, and the 7-day warning message posts correctly.
implementation_plan:
1) Create Jira space 'Observability Platform' (OPS template) and set key OBS-; configure projects settings, workflows, and issue types.
2) Build Confluence page template in sandbox space, run review with SRE and Platform leads, then push to production.
3) Provision identity groups in Okta (obs-pod-*-edit & obs-pod-*-read) and map to Jira/Confluence roles.
4) Develop two automations in the automation platform: (A) Slack-bot-rotate job using KMS + CI pipeline to rotate token and update the bot deployment; (B) Slack-channel-archive job using channel activity metrics + message job. Add feature flags for staged rollout.
5) QA in staging: create test issue, test template, run token rotation pipeline with a simulated secret, run archive on a test channel.
6) Schedule rollout: enable for obs-pod-core first, then incrementally onboard other pods.
7) Create runbook and schedule a 30-day follow-up review after initial rollout.
rollout_notes: Start in staging (us-east) for obs-pod-core. After 72 hours validated, enable in us-east prod. After 2 weeks, enable eu-west. Notify #support and #sre channels ahead of each rollout.
